#1
L: Again indeed, O great-armed-one, hear my supreme word — which to-you, dear, I-shall-declare, out-of-a-wish-for-benefit.
I: Once again, Mahābāho, hear my supreme word, which I will speak to you, so dear to me, for your benefit.
N: Kṛṣṇa resumes the teaching begun in chapter 9 (bhūyaḥ eva, 'once again'); yat, 'which', looks back to vacaḥ, 'word', already named in pāda a — the very word he is about to speak. Mahābāho, 'great-armed one', addresses Arjuna. Sandhi: भूय is bhūyaḥ with its visarga dropped before the vowel e- of eva (-aḥ + e- → -a e-, the rule for a visarga before any vowel but a-); यत्तेऽहं packs yat+te (-t+t-→-tt-) + aham (avagraha, -e+a-→-e).
#2
L: Not my origin the-hosts-of-gods know, nor the-great-sages; I [am] the-origin indeed of-the-gods and-of-the-great-sages, in-every-way.
I: Neither the hosts of the gods know my origin, nor the great sages; for I am, in every respect, the origin of the gods and of the great sages.
N: A double negative parallel (na ... na) states that no one — not even gods or great sages — knows Kṛṣṇa's prabhava, 'origin, source', because he precedes them all (ahamādir hi, 'for I am the origin'); this opens the chapter's argument for his unoriginated nature, continued through verse 3. Sandhi: महर्षयः and महर्षीणां both pack mahā+ṛṣi (ā+ṛ→ar), a compound recurring often in this chapter; अहमादिर्हि packs aham+ādiḥ, joined, +hi (-iḥ+h-→-ir h-).
#3
L: Who me, the-unborn and-the-beginningless, knows, the-great-lord-of-the-world — undeluded he among-mortals, from-all-sins is-released.
I: He who knows me as unborn and without beginning, the great lord of the world — that man, undeluded among mortals, is freed from all sins.
N: A relative-correlative construction (yaḥ, 'who' ... saḥ, 'that one'), the standard Gītā pattern for stating a general rule: whoever truly knows Kṛṣṇa as aja, 'unborn', and anādi, 'beginningless' — the point just established in verse 2 — is thereby freed. Loka-mahā-īśvaram, 'the great lord of the world' (ā+ī→e), is in apposition to mām. Sandhi: यो is yaḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o. Note also that the pronoun saḥ ('he') in the second line loses its visarga to sa before the following consonant m-, not to -o as महर्षयः did in verse 2 — sa and eṣa are irregular this way before any consonant, unlike ordinary nouns and adjectives.
#4
L: Intellect, knowledge, freedom-from-delusion, patience, truth, self-restraint, tranquility; happiness, pain, existence, non-existence, fear and-fearlessness-too, and—
I: Intellect, knowledge, freedom from delusion, patience, truth, self-control, tranquility; happiness, sorrow, coming-to-be, ceasing-to-be, fear and fearlessness too—
N: The first of two verses (continuing through verse 5's first line) listing the states of mind and being that arise from Kṛṣṇa alone; all these nominals are subjects of bhavanti, 'they arise', in verse 5's second line, and the sentence is only completed there. Each term is translated individually (none of these — buddhi, jñāna, saṃmoha, kṣamā, and so on — is on the small untranslated-terms list of dharma/yoga/brahman/guṇa/sāṃkhya). Sandhi: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः packs buddhiḥ+jñānam (-iḥ+j-→-ir j-) + asaṃmohaḥ, joined; भवोऽभावो packs bhavaḥ+abhāvaḥ (avagraha), whose own visarga then becomes -o before the voiced bh- of bhayam; चाभयमेव packs ca+abhayam (a+a→ā) + eva, joined.
#5
L: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, generosity, fame and-ill-fame; they-arise, [these] dispositions, of-beings, from-me alone, of-manifold-kinds.
I: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame and disgrace — these various dispositions of beings arise from me alone, each in its own form.
N: This completes the sentence begun at verse 4: bhavanti, 'they arise', is the verb governing every noun listed there and in this verse's first line, all of them bhāvāḥ, 'dispositions, states', of bhūtānām, 'of beings', which come pṛthag-vidhāḥ, 'in manifold forms', mattaḥ eva, 'from me alone' — Kṛṣṇa is the single source of every mental and existential state, both the exalted (buddhi, jñāna...) and its opposite (duḥkham, ayaśaḥ...). Sandhi: तुष्टिस्तपो packs tuṣṭiḥ+tapaḥ (-iḥ+t-→-is t-, a visarga before a voiceless stop keeps -s rather than voicing to -r), whose own -aḥ then becomes -o before the voiced d- of dānam; यशोऽयशः packs yaśaḥ+ayaśaḥ (avagraha); भावा is bhāvāḥ with its visarga dropped (not -o) before the voiced bh- of bhūtānām, the same -āḥ pattern noted at verses 2-3 for the long-ā plural.
#6
L: The-great-sages, seven, ancient, four Manus likewise, of-my-nature, mind-born, born — of-whom [is] the-world['s], these, creatures.
I: The seven great sages of old, and the four Manus as well, share my nature and were born of my mind; from them come these creatures of the world.
N: Kṛṣṇa now names, as instances of the mad-bhāvāḥ, 'states sprung from me', just listed in verses 4-5, the maharṣayaḥ sapta, 'seven great sages' (the traditional saptarṣi), and the four Manus, primal ancestors of mankind, all mānasāḥ jātāḥ, 'born of [Kṛṣṇa's] mind' — from whom in turn all present creatures descend. Sandhi: चत्वारो is catvāraḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o; मनवस्तथा packs manavaḥ+tathā (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); मद्भावा, मानसा and जाता each show a visarga (-āḥ, long-ā plural) simply dropping before the following voiced consonant, without becoming -o, the pattern first seen at verse 2's पुरुषा-type forms; लोक is lokaḥ with its own -aḥ dropping before the vowel इ- of imāḥ.
#7
L: This manifestation and-yoga of-mine, who truly knows — he with-unwavering yoga is-united; no-doubt here.
I: Whoever truly knows this manifestation and yoga of mine is united with me in unwavering yoga — of this there is no doubt.
N: Vibhūti, 'manifestation, extraordinary power', names the chapter's subject directly for the first time (it recurs as the chapter's title-word and again at verse 40); yoga here is Kṛṣṇa's own creative power of self-manifestation, kept untranslated like the yoga of other chapters, though the sense shades toward 'miraculous power' rather than disciplined practice. Sandhi: यो is yaḥ, -aḥ before v- → -o; सोऽविकम्पेन packs saḥ+avikampena (avagraha); नात्र packs na+atra (a+a→ā).
#8
L: I of-all [am] the-origin; from-me all proceeds — thus having-considered, worship me the-wise, endowed-with-feeling.
I: I am the source of all; from me everything proceeds. Understanding this, the wise, filled with devotion, worship me.
N: This states directly the claim verses 2-7 have been building toward: Kṛṣṇa is sarvasya prabhavaḥ, 'the origin of all', so that the wise (budhāḥ) who grasp this (iti matvā, 'having understood thus') respond with bhajana, 'devotional worship' — a term distinct from the jñāna, 'knowledge', of the preceding verses, marking the turn from cosmology to devotion continued through verse 11. Sandhi: प्रभवो is prabhavaḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o; बुधा is budhāḥ with its visarga dropped (not -o) before the voiced bh- of bhāva-samanvitāḥ, the same -āḥ pattern seen through this chapter.
#9
L: With-minds-on-me, with-life-breaths-absorbed-in-me, enlightening one-another, and-speaking-of [me] constantly, [they are] content and they-delight.
I: With their minds fixed on me, their very life-breath absorbed in me, they enlighten one another and constantly speak of me; they find contentment and take delight.
N: This begins the chapter's portrait of the bhaktas, Kṛṣṇa's devotees (continued through verse 11), described first through two bahuvrīhi compounds, mac-cittāḥ and mad-gata-prāṇāḥ ('whose minds/life-breath are on me'), then through the mutual community of devotion — bodhayantaḥ parasparam, 'enlightening each other' — an ideal picture of satsaṅga, the company of the like-minded. Sandhi: मच्चित्ता packs mat+cittāḥ (-t+c-→-cc-), its own visarga then dropping before the voiced m- of madgataprāṇāḥ; मद्गतप्राणा packs mat+gata (-t+g-→-d g-) +prāṇāḥ, its visarga likewise dropping before the voiced b- of bodhayantaḥ; कथयन्तश्च is kathayantaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-, the pattern already seen at 9.14's यतन्तश्च).
#10
L: To-them, constantly-disciplined, worshiping, lovingly, I-give the-yoga-of-understanding, that, by-which to-me they-come, they.
I: To them, ever disciplined, who worship me with love, I give the yoga of understanding by which they come to me.
N: This answers verse 9's portrait of the devotee with Kṛṣṇa's own promise: buddhi-yogam, 'the yoga of understanding' (or 'discriminative wisdom', cf. its earlier sense at 2.49 and 3.3; buddhi itself is translated, yoga kept untranslated), is given as a gift (dadāmi, 'I give') to those who worship prīti-pūrvakam, 'with love'. Sandhi: मामुपयान्ति packs mām+upayānti, joined, with no phonetic change since mām ends in the consonant -m.
#11
L: Of-them alone, out-of-compassion, I, ignorance-born darkness — abiding-in-their-being, I-destroy, with-the-lamp-of-knowledge, radiant.
I: Out of compassion for them alone, I, abiding within their being, destroy with the radiant lamp of knowledge the darkness born of ignorance.
N: Kṛṣṇa completes the promise of verse 10: the buddhi-yoga given to the devotees works by destroying (nāśayāmi) their ajñāna-jam tamaḥ, 'the darkness born of ignorance', from within — ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ, 'abiding in their [inner] being' — with the jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā, 'radiant lamp of knowledge'. The whole first line is one long run of words joined purely by -m before a following vowel, with no phonetic change at any boundary. Sandhi: नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो packs nāśayāmi+ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ (-i+ā-→-y ā-), whose own -aḥ then becomes -o before the voiced j- of jñānadīpena.
#12
L: The-supreme brahman, the-supreme abode, the-pure, the-supreme, [are] you; the-person, eternal, divine, the-primal-god, unborn, all-pervading —
I: You are the supreme brahman, the supreme abode, the pure, the supreme; the eternal, divine Person, the primal god, unborn, all-pervading —
N: Arjuna's great eulogy of Kṛṣṇa begins here, one long sentence spanning verses 12-13. This verse's first line is complete in itself: bhavān, 'you' (honorific), is said to be paraṃ brahma, 'the supreme brahman' (kept untranslated), and paraṃ dhāma, 'the supreme abode' — neuter nominal predicates used of the addressee, fitting for praise of the Absolute. The second line shifts to accusative forms (puruṣam, śāśvatam...) that are not governed by anything in this verse: they become the object complements of āhus tvām, 'they call you', which opens verse 13, so the two verses form a single sentence — a construction flagged here rather than repeated at verse 13. No sandhi splits words within this verse; दिव्यमादिदेवमजं simply strings three words together with -m written joined before each following vowel, with no phonetic change.
#13
L: [You] the-sages all call, the-divine-sage Nārada likewise; Asita, Devala, Vyāsa, and-yourself indeed you-declare to-me.
I: All the sages call you so, as does the divine sage Nārada; so do Asita, Devala and Vyāsa — and you yourself tell me so.
N: This completes the sentence begun in verse 12: āhuḥ tvām, 'they call you', governs all the accusative epithets of verse 12's second line; the list of authorities continues with devarṣiḥ Nāradaḥ ('the divine sage Nārada', a celestial seer and messenger of the gods), Asita and Devala (sages traditionally paired together), and Vyāsa (the sage credited with compiling the Vedas and composing the Mahābhārata itself), closing with Kṛṣṇa's own testimony, svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me, 'and you yourself tell me so'. Sandhi: आहुस्त्वामृषयः packs āhuḥ+tvām (-uḥ+t-→-us t-) +ṛṣayaḥ, joined; देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा packs deva+ṛṣiḥ (a+ṛ→ar) +Nāradaḥ (-iḥ+n-→-ir n-) +tathā (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); असितो and देवलो both show -aḥ before a voiced consonant → -o; चैव is ca+eva (a+e→ai).
#14
L: All this true I-believe, which to-me you-tell, O-slayer-of-Keśin; for not your, O-Lord, manifestation know the-gods, nor the-demons.
I: I believe all this to be true, Keśava, which you tell me; for, O Lord, neither the gods nor the demons know your true manifestation.
N: Arjuna closes his eulogy by affirming as ṛtam, 'true', everything Kṛṣṇa has told him, then adds his own observation: not even the gods or the dānavāḥ, 'demons, titans', know Kṛṣṇa's vyaktim, 'manifestation, true nature' — the very term the chapter's remaining verses go on to unfold. Keśava and bhagavan both address Kṛṣṇa directly. Sandhi: सर्वमेतदृतं packs sarvam+etat (joined) +ṛtam (-t+ṛ-→-d ṛ-); यन्मां is yat+mām (-t+m-→-n m-); विदुर्देवा packs viduḥ+devāḥ (-uḥ+d-→-ur d-), whose own visarga then drops before the voiced n- of na.
#15
L: By-yourself indeed with-your-own-self your-own-self you-know, you, O-supreme-person, O-origin-of-beings, O-lord-of-beings, O-god-of-gods, O-lord-of-the-world.
I: You alone truly know yourself, by yourself, O supreme Person, source of beings, lord of beings, god of gods, lord of the world.
N: Arjuna opens the second half of his eulogy (through v.18) by observing that only Kṛṣṇa can know himself, since he precedes and exceeds all other knowers — the reflexive svayam eva ātmanā ātmānam, 'you yourself, by your own self, [know] your own self', piles up the same pronoun three times for emphasis. The four vocatives that follow are all epithets of Kṛṣṇa: puruṣottama, 'supreme Person' (recalling puruṣam at 10.12); bhūtabhāvana, 'originator of beings' (bhāvana, causative of bhū); bhūteśa, 'lord of beings'; devadeva, 'god of gods'; jagatpate, 'lord of the world'. Sandhi: स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं packs eva+ātmanā (a+ā→ā) and ātmanā+ātmānam (ā+ā→ā, no visible change since both are already long); भूतेश packs bhūta+īśa (a+ī→e).
#16
L: To-declare you-ought, without-remainder, [your] divine indeed self-manifestations; by-which manifestations these worlds you, having-pervaded, abide.
I: You should declare in full your divine manifestations, by which you pervade and abide in these worlds.
N: aśeṣeṇa, 'without remainder, exhaustively', qualifies vaktum arhasi, 'you ought to declare'; ātma-vibhūtayaḥ, 'your own manifestations', takes up the chapter's title-word vibhūti (cf. v.7) and turns it toward the catalog about to follow; the relative clause yābhiḥ...vyāpya tiṣṭhasi, 'by which...you pervade and abide', likewise anticipates that list. Sandhi: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण packs vaktum+arhasi (joined) + aśeṣeṇa (-i+a-→-ya, the glide-formation already seen at 10.11 before ā, here before short a); दिव्या is divyāḥ with visarga dropped before the voiced h- of hi (the -āḥ pattern recurring since 10.2); ह्यात्मविभूतयः packs hi+ātma-vibhūtayaḥ (-i+ā-→-y ā-, as at 10.11); याभिर्विभूतिभिर् packs yābhiḥ+vibhūtibhiḥ (-iḥ+v-→-ir v-); लोकानिमांस्त्वं packs lokān+imān (joined) +tvam (-n+t-→-ṃs t-, a new pattern: word-final -n before t-/th- inserts -s-, giving -ṃs t-).
#17
L: How may-I-know I, O-yogin, you, always meditating; in-which, in-which and states are-you-to-be-meditated-on, O-lord, by-me?
I: How may I know you, master of yoga, always meditating on you? And in which states of being am I to contemplate you, my Lord?
N: vidyām, an optative ('may I know'), governs the whole question; yogin addresses Kṛṣṇa as master of yoga; keṣu keṣu, 'in which, in which', a reduplication distributing over bhāveṣu, 'states of being' — 'in each of the various states'; cintyaḥ asi, gerundive plus copula, 'you are to be meditated upon'. Sandhi: योगिंस्त्वां packs yogin+tvām (-n+t-→-ṃs t-, as at 10.16); चिन्त्योऽसि packs cintyaḥ+asi (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha, as at 10.4, 10.5, 10.7).
#18
L: At-length your-own yoga and-manifestation, O-rouser-of-men; again speak — satiety indeed of-[me]-listening there-is-not, for-me, [this] nectar.
I: Tell me again in full detail, Janārdana, of your yoga and your manifestation; for I never tire of hearing this nectar.
N: Arjuna's fourfold question (vv.15-18) closes by asking Kṛṣṇa to speak bhūyaḥ, 'again', and vistareṇa, 'at length' — the very fullness he had already asked for with aśeṣeṇa at v.16 — since the amṛtam, 'nectar', of this teaching never satisfies him (tṛptiḥ...na asti, 'there is no satiety'). Janārdana, 'rouser' or 'tormentor of men', is an epithet of Kṛṣṇa. Sandhi: विस्तरेणात्मनो packs vistareṇa+ātmanaḥ (a+ā→ā), whose own visarga becomes -o before the voiced y- of yogam; तृप्तिर्हि packs tṛptiḥ+hi (-iḥ+h-→-ir h-, the same voicing seen in devarṣir nāradas at 10.13); शृण्वतो is śṛṇvataḥ, -aḥ before n- → -o; नास्ति packs na+asti (a+a→ā); मेऽमृतम् packs me+amṛtam (avagraha).
#19
L: Well-then, to-you I-will-declare [my] divine indeed self-manifestations, chiefly, O-best-of-the-Kurus; there-is-no-end of-my extent.
I: Very well, Kuruśreṣṭha — I will declare to you my divine manifestations, but only the chief ones; there is no end to my extent.
N: Kṛṣṇa answers Arjuna's fourfold question (vv.15-18) and opens the great catalog of vibhūtis that runs to v.42; prādhānyataḥ, 'by way of the chief ones', concedes that only the principal manifestations can be told, since — as the second line states, and as v.40 will state again — his vistara, 'extent', has no end. Kuruśreṣṭha, 'best of the Kurus', addresses Arjuna. Sandhi: दिव्या and ह्यात्मविभूतयः repeat 10.16's pattern; नास्त्यन्तो packs na+asti (a+a→ā) +antaḥ (-i+a-→-ya, as at 10.16), whose own visarga becomes -o before the voiced v- of vistarasya.
#20
L: I [am] the-self, O-lord-of-sleep, seated-in-the-heart of-all-beings; I [am] the-beginning and the-middle and, of-beings, the-end too.
I: I am the Self, Guḍākeśa, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of beings as well.
N: This opens the catalog proper (through v.42): Kṛṣṇa first identifies himself with the universal ātman, 'Self', dwelling in every creature's āśaya, 'seat, heart', then states his cosmic completeness as beginning, middle and end of beings — a claim echoed again at v.32. Guḍākeśa, 'lord of sleep', is an epithet of Arjuna. Sandhi: सर्वभूताशयस्थितः packs bhūta+āśaya (a+ā→ā); अहमादिश्च packs aham+ādiḥ (joined) +ca (-iḥ+c-→-iś c-, as kathayantaś ca at 10.9); भूतानामन्त packs bhūtānām+antaḥ, its visarga dropping before the vowel e- of eva exactly as bhūyaḥ eva did at 10.1 (-aḥ + non-a vowel → -a, with no further merging of the resulting a with the following vowel).
#21
L: Of-the-Ādityas I [am] Viṣṇu, of-lights the-sun, radiant; of-the-Maruts Marīci I-am, of-constellations I [am] the-moon.
I: Of the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; of lights, the radiant sun; of the Maruts, Marīci; of the constellations, the moon.
N: The catalog's basic pattern appears here for the first time in its full form: a class named in the genitive plural, and Kṛṣṇa identified with its foremost member ('of X, I am Y'); the pattern recurs through v.42, growing terser as it repeats, and is not re-explained at each occurrence. The Ādityas are the twelve solar deities, sons of Aditi, among whom Viṣṇu is reckoned chief; the Maruts are the storm-gods, here led by the sage Marīci (elsewhere counted among the seven great sages, cf. 10.6). Sandhi: विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां and मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि both voice a final -iḥ/-uḥ to -ir/-ur before a following voiced sound, the pattern recurring through this chapter (e.g. 10.13, 10.18); रविरंशुमान् likewise voices -iḥ to -ir before the vowel a-.
#22
L: Of-the-Vedas the-Sāmaveda I-am; of-gods I-am Vāsava; of-the-senses the-mind and-I-am; of-beings I-am consciousness.
I: Of the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; of the gods, Vāsava (Indra); of the senses, the mind; of beings, consciousness.
N: Vāsava, 'lord of the Vasus', is a name of Indra, king of the gods. Sandhi: सामवेदोऽस्मि packs sāmavedaḥ+asmi (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha, as at 10.17); मनश्चास्मि packs manaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) +asmi (a+a→ā).
#23
L: Of-the-Rudras Śaṅkara and-I-am, the-lord-of-wealth of-yakṣas-and-rākṣasas; of-the-Vasus Pāvaka and-I-am, Meru of-peaked-mountains I.
I: Of the Rudras I am Śaṅkara (Śiva); of yakṣas and rākṣasas, the lord of wealth (Kubera); of the Vasus, Pāvaka (Agni); of the peaked mountains, Meru.
N: Śaṅkara is a name of Śiva, head of the eleven Rudras; Vitteśa, 'lord of wealth', names Kubera, treasurer of the gods and overlord of yakṣas and rākṣasas; Pāvaka, 'purifier', is a name of Agni, chief of the eight Vasus; Meru is the cosmic mountain at the world's axis. Sandhi: शंकरश्चास्मि and पावकश्चास्मि both pack -aḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) +asmi (a+a→ā), as at v.22; वित्तेशो packs vitta+īśa (a+ī→e), its visarga becoming -o before the voiced y- of yakṣarakṣasām.
#24
L: Of-household-priests and the-chief me know, O-son-of-Pṛthā, Bṛhaspati; of-army-commanders I [am] Skanda, of-bodies-of-water I-am the-ocean.
I: And know me to be Bṛhaspati, chief of household priests, Pārtha; of army commanders I am Skanda; of lakes I am the ocean.
N: Bṛhaspati, preceptor and chief priest of the gods, is here named foremost among purodhasaḥ, 'household priests'; Skanda (Kārttikeya) leads the gods' armies as senānī. Pārtha, 'son of Pṛthā [Kuntī]', addresses Arjuna. No sandhi splits any word in this verse; each token is simply written joined before its following vowel with no phonetic change (senānīnām+aham, sarasām+asmi).
#25
L: Of-the-great-sages Bhṛgu I; of-utterances I-am the-single syllable; of-sacrifices the-sacrifice-of-silent-repetition I-am, of-immovable-things the-Himālaya.
I: Of the great sages I am Bhṛgu; of utterances, the single syllable Oṃ; of sacrifices, the sacrifice of silent recitation; of immovable things, the Himālaya.
N: Bhṛgu, one of the seven great sages (mahaṛṣi), a group referenced generally at 10.6; the 'single syllable' (ekam akṣaram) is the sacred Oṃ, held to be the essence of all speech; japa-yajña, 'the sacrifice of silently repeating [a mantra]', is ranked here above outward ritual sacrifice. Sandhi: महर्षीणां packs mahā+ṛṣīṇām (ā+ṛ→ar, as before); भृगुरहं shows -uḥ+a-→-ur a-; गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् packs girām+asmi (joined) +ekam (-i+e-→-y e-, the same glide mechanism as -i+a-/-i+ā- at 10.11 and 10.16, here before e-) +akṣaram (joined); जपयज्ञोऽस्मि packs japayajñaḥ+asmi (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha).
#26
L: The-sacred-fig-tree, of-all-trees; and-of-divine-sages, Nārada; of-gandharvas, Citraratha; of-siddhas, the-sage Kapila.
I: Of all trees I am the sacred fig; of divine sages, Nārada; of gandharvas, Citraratha; of siddhas, the sage Kapila.
N: Nārada, the celestial sage and divine messenger, already named among Kṛṣṇa's witnesses at 10.13; Citraratha is traditionally king of the gandharvas, the celestial musicians; the siddhas are perfected beings of supernatural power, among whom Kapila — traditionally credited as founder of the Sāṃkhya system (cf. 2.39) — is named foremost. Sandhi: देवर्षीणां packs deva+ṛṣīṇām (a+ṛ→ar); कपिलो shows -aḥ before m- → -o, as elsewhere in this chapter.
#27
L: Uccaiḥśravas, of-horses, know me, arisen-from-the-nectar-of-immortality; Airāvata, of-lordly-elephants, of-men and the-king.
I: Know me, of horses, to be Uccaiḥśravas, sprung from the nectar of immortality; of lordly elephants, Airāvata; and of men, the king.
N: Uccaiḥśravas, the divine horse, and Airāvata, Indra's elephant, both arose from the amṛta-manthana, the churning of the ocean of milk by gods and demons for the nectar of immortality — the myth the epithet amṛtodbhavam, 'sprung from the nectar', recalls. Sandhi: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां and माममृतोद्भवम् both show final -m simply written joined before a following vowel with no phonetic change; within the latter, amṛta+udbhavam shows a+u→o; गजेन्द्राणां packs gaja+indrāṇām (a+i→e); नराधिपम् packs nara+adhipam (joined, no change).
#28
L: Of-weapons I [am] the-thunderbolt, of-cows I-am the-wish-fulfilling-cow; the-progenitor and-I-am, Kandarpa; of-serpents I-am Vāsuki.
I: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; of cows, the wish-fulfilling cow (Kāmadhenu); I am the progenitor, Kandarpa (the god of love); of serpents, Vāsuki.
N: Kāmadhuk, 'yielding every desire', names Kāmadhenu, the wish-fulfilling cow born — like Uccaiḥśravas and Airāvata in the previous verse — at the churning of the ocean; Kandarpa is another name of Kāma, the god of love, here called prajanaḥ, 'the begetter', as the personified desire that generates all beings; Vāsuki is the great serpent-king. Sandhi: प्रजनश्चास्मि packs prajanaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) +asmi (a+a→ā), as at vv.22-23.
#29
L: Ananta and-I-am, of-nāgas; Varuṇa, of-water-deities, I; of-ancestors Aryaman and-I-am, Yama, of-restrainers, I.
I: Of the nāgas I am Ananta; of water-deities, Varuṇa; of ancestors, Aryaman; of those who administer law, Yama.
N: Ananta is Śeṣa, the cosmic serpent-king on whom Viṣṇu reclines between cycles of creation, here named chief among nāgas, the serpent-deities; Varuṇa presides over the waters and yādāṃsi, water-creatures; Aryaman, one of the twelve Ādityas, is associated with ancestors and the sacred order; Yama, god of death, is named foremost among saṃyamatām, 'those who restrain, administer law'. Sandhi: अनन्तश्चास्मि and चास्मि both pack -aḥ+c-→-aś c- and/or ca+asmi (a+a→ā), as regularly since v.22; वरुणो shows -aḥ before y- → -o.
#30
L: Prahlāda and-I-am, of-daityas; Time, of-calculators, I; of-beasts and lord-of-beasts I, and-Vainateya, of-birds.
I: Of the daityas I am Prahlāda; of calculators, Time; of beasts, the lion; and of birds, Vainateya (Garuḍa).
N: Prahlāda, the devout daitya king rescued by Viṣṇu's Narasiṃha incarnation from his demon father Hiraṇyakaśipu, is named chief of the daityas, just as at v.23 Śiva was named chief of the Rudras; kālaḥ, 'Time', recurs from the famous 11.32 (kept capitalized here as there, the house rendering); mṛgendra, 'lord of beasts', is the lion; Vainateya, 'son of Vinatā', is Garuḍa, king of the birds and Viṣṇu's mount. Sandhi: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि and वैनतेयश्च both pack -aḥ+c-→-aś c-; मृगेन्द्रोऽहं packs the compound mṛga+indra (a+i→e) then mṛgendraḥ+aham (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha).
#31
L: The-wind, of-purifiers, I-am; Rāma, of-weapon-bearers, I; of-fish and makara-I-am, of-rivers I-am Jāhnavī.
I: Of purifiers I am the wind; of weapon-bearers, Rāma; of fish, the makara; and of rivers, the Gaṅgā.
N: pavana, 'wind', is named foremost among pavatām, 'purifying things'; Rāma is ambiguous — commentators read it as either Paraśurāma, the axe-wielding warrior-brāhmaṇa and sixth avatāra of Viṣṇu, or Rāmacandra, hero of the Rāmāyaṇa and seventh avatāra, and the verse gives no way to decide between them. makara is a mythical sea-monster or crocodile; Jāhnavī, 'daughter of Jahnu' (the sage said to have once swallowed and then released the river), is a name of the Gaṅgā (Ganges). Sandhi: मकरश्चास्मि packs -aḥ+c-→-aś c- + a+a→ā, as regularly.
#32
L: Of-creations the-beginning and-the-end, and the-middle indeed, I-am, Arjuna; of-sciences the-science-of-the-individual-self, of-debaters the-debate, I.
I: Of creations I am the beginning, the end, and the middle too, Arjuna; of sciences, the science of the individual self; of debaters, the argument.
N: sarga, 'creation, emanation', restates of every act of creation the beginning-middle-end claim already made at v.20; adhyātma-vidyā, 'the science of the self' in the verse's own gloss — adhyātma, 'pertaining to the self', whose fixed English rendering (set at 8.3's review) is 'the individual self' — is named foremost among vidyā, 'branches of knowledge'; vāda, 'reasoned argument, debate', is likewise claimed among pravadatām, 'debaters, disputants'. Sandhi: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च packs sargāṇām+ādiḥ (joined, no change) +antaḥ (-iḥ+a-→-ir a-) +ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); चैवाहमर्जुन packs ca+eva (a+e→ai) +aham (a+a→ā) +arjuna (joined, no change); अध्यात्मविद्या packs adhi+ātman (i+ā→y ā, the same glide formation as -i+ā- at 10.11, 10.16, here compound-internally).
#33
L: Of-letters the-[syllable]-A I-am, the-dvandva of-compounds and; I-alone imperishable Time, the-ordainer-I facing-every-direction.
I: Of letters I am the letter A; and of compounds, the dvandva; I alone am imperishable Time; I am the ordainer, facing every direction.
N: akāra, the syllable A, is held to be the seed of all speech, as Oṃ was at v.25; dvandva, the 'pair' or copulative compound (e.g. Rāma-Lakṣmaṇau, 'Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa'), is named foremost among sāmāsika, 'compound words', a piece of Sanskrit grammatical terminology; akṣayaḥ kālaḥ, 'imperishable Time', echoes the kālaḥ of v.30 and the famous kālaḥ of 11.32 (the house rendering kept here too); dhātṛ, 'ordainer, creator', with viśvatas-mukhaḥ, 'facing every direction', recalls the four-faced creator Brahmā of tradition, here claimed by Kṛṣṇa himself. Sandhi: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि packs -aḥ+a-→-o- (avagraha), as regularly; अहमेवाक्षयः packs eva+akṣayaḥ (a+a→ā); कालो shows -aḥ before dh-→-o; धाताहं shows ā+a→ā (dhātā+aham); विश्वतोमुखः is a compound whose internal visarga voices to -o before the consonant m-, as with kapilaḥ muniḥ at 10.26.
#34
L: Death, the-all-seizer-and-I-am, and-the-origin, of-things-to-come; Fame, Fortune-and-Speech, of-feminine[-things], Memory, Intelligence, Firmness, Patience.
I: I am death, the all-seizer, and the origin of things to come; and, among feminine qualities, fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, firmness, and patience.
N: sarva-haraḥ, 'seizer of all', names death as the universal taker; udbhava, 'arising', paired with bhaviṣyatām, 'of things to come', names Kṛṣṇa as the source, the rising prosperity, of what is yet to be. The list that follows names seven famous feminine-gender nouns — kīrti (fame), śrī (fortune, beauty), vāk (speech), smṛti (memory), medhā (intelligence), dhṛti (steadfastness), kṣamā (patience) — traditionally personified as goddesses, all identified with Kṛṣṇa under the marker nārīṇām, 'of feminine [qualities]'. Sandhi: सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च packs sarvaharaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) +aham (a+a→ā; joined before u-, no change) +udbhavaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); श्रीर्वाक्च packs śrīḥ+vāk (-īḥ+v-→-īr v-, the same -iḥ/-īḥ voicing pattern as elsewhere, here on a long vowel); स्मृतिर्मेधा packs smṛtiḥ+medhā (-iḥ+m-→-ir m-).
#35
L: The-Bṛhatsāman, thus, of-hymns; the-Gāyatrī of-metres I; of-months Mārgaśīrṣa-I, of-seasons the-flower-bearer.
I: Of hymns I am, thus, the Bṛhatsāman; of metres, the Gāyatrī; of months, Mārgaśīrṣa; of seasons, the flower-bearer (spring).
N: the Bṛhatsāman is a celebrated Sāmavedic melody; the Gāyatrī, most sacred of Vedic metres, is the metre of the famous Gāyatrī mantra; Mārgaśīrṣa (November–December) is reckoned the first and most auspicious month of the traditional calendar; kusumākara, 'the flower-abundance', personifies spring, the season of flowering. Sandhi: मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां packs mārgaśīrṣaḥ+aham (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha) +ṛtūnām (joined, no change); कुसुमाकरः packs kusuma+ākara (a+ā→ā).
#36
L: The-gambling, of-cheats, I-am; splendor, of-the-splendid, I; victory-I-am, resolve-I-am, goodness, of-the-virtuous, I.
I: I am the gambling of cheats; I am the splendor of the splendid; I am victory, I am resolve; I am the goodness of the virtuous.
N: chalayatām, 'of those who deceive, cheats', names gambling as their characteristic activity, claimed here as Kṛṣṇa's own — a startling inclusion in the catalog, matched by other morally ambiguous items already claimed (Time as death-dealer at v.30, the rod of punishment to come at v.38); sattvam here is 'goodness' in its ordinary sense (courage, virtue, integrity), not the technical guṇa of that name, as the pairing with sattvavatām, 'the virtuous', makes clear. Sandhi: तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् shows tejaḥ's visarga realized as -as before the voiceless t- of tejasvinām, the same pattern seen at 10.6's manavas tathā; जयोऽस्मि and व्यवसायोऽस्मि both show -aḥ+a-→-o- (avagraha), as regularly.
#37
L: Of-the-Vṛṣṇis Vāsudeva-I-am; of-the-Pāṇḍavas Dhanañjaya; of-sages even-I [am] Vyāsa; of-poets Uśanas the-poet.
I: Of the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva; of the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanañjaya (Arjuna); of sages, even I am Vyāsa; of poets, the poet Uśanas.
N: Vāsudeva, Kṛṣṇa's own patronymic, names him foremost of his clan, the Vṛṣṇis — Kṛṣṇa identifying with himself; Dhanañjaya, 'winner of wealth', is Arjuna's own epithet, addressed here as if from outside, naming him best of the Pāṇḍavas; Vyāsa is the sage traditionally credited with compiling the Vedas and composing the Mahābhārata itself, the very poem in which this verse occurs; Uśanas, also called Śukra, is preceptor of the demons and a renowned poet-sage — his name here keeps an archaic nominative in -ā rather than the expected -āḥ. Sandhi: वासुदेवोऽस्मि shows -aḥ+a-→-o- (avagraha); मुनीनामप्यहं packs munīnām+api (joined) +aham (-i+a-→-y a-, the glide formation seen since 10.11).
#38
L: The-rod, of-those-who-subdue, I-am; the-policy I-am, of-those-who-seek-victory; the-silence and-indeed-I-am, of-secret-things; the-knowledge, of-those-who-have-knowledge, I.
I: Of those who subdue, I am the rod of punishment; of those who seek victory, I am statesmanship; of secret things, I am silence; and of those who have knowledge, I am knowledge.
N: daṇḍa, 'the rod', names the coercive power of punishment wielded by those who chastise, damayatām; nīti, 'statecraft, prudent policy', is claimed among jigīṣatām, 'those who desire victory'; mauna, 'silence', is named the foremost of guhyāni, 'secret, hidden things' — silence as the deepest form of keeping a secret; this verse closes the catalog's ethical and political items before the summarizing verses that follow. Sandhi: दण्डो shows -aḥ before d- → -o; नीतिरस्मि shows -iḥ+a-→-ir a-; चैवास्मि packs ca+eva (a+e→ai) +asmi (a+a→ā), as at v.32.
#39
L: And-which even, of-all-beings, the-seed, that-I-am, Arjuna; not that exists, without-which, might-be by-me, being moving-or-unmoving.
I: Whatever is the seed of all beings, that am I, Arjuna; there is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without me.
N: The catalog's individual items give way here to a general claim, closing the list proper before the summary of vv.40-42: whatever bījam, 'seed', underlies any being at all, Kṛṣṇa is that seed; the relative-correlative yat...tat construction ('whatever...that') states the identity, and the second relative clause (yat syāt) extends it to every being whatsoever, cara-acaram, 'moving or unmoving' — the standard Sanskrit merism for the whole of creation, animate and inanimate alike. Sandhi: यच्चापि packs yat+ca (-t+c-→-cc-) +api (a+a→ā); तदहमर्जुन and तदस्ति both show tat+a-→-d a- (dental voicing before a vowel); यत्स्यान्मया packs yat+syāt (joined) +mayā (-t+m-→-n m-, the same assimilation of word-final -t before m- seen at 10.14's yan mām); चराचरम् packs cara+acaram (a+a→ā).
#40
L: Not-the-end-there-is of-my divine of-manifestations, O-scorcher-of-foes; this but by-way-of-indication declared, of-manifestation the-extent, by-me.
I: There is no end to my divine manifestations, Parantapa; this is but a sample I have stated of the extent of my manifestation.
N: This verse begins the closing movement (through v.42), declaring the preceding catalog merely uddeśataḥ, 'by way of indication, as a sample' — an illustrative fraction, not an exhaustive list, of Kṛṣṇa's vistara, 'extent', a term picking up prabhavaḥ vistaraḥ ca from v.18 and vistaro mama of v.19. Parantapa, 'scorcher of foes', addresses Arjuna. Sandhi: नान्तोऽस्ति packs na+antaḥ (a+a→ā) +asti (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha); तूद्देशतः packs tu+uddeśataḥ (u+u→ū); प्रोक्तो shows -aḥ before v-→-o; विभूतेर्विस्तरो packs vibhūteḥ+vistaraḥ (-eḥ+v-→-er v-), whose own visarga becomes -o before the voiced m- of mayā.
#41
L: Whatever glorious being, splendid or mighty; that-that indeed-understand you, my of-splendor a-fraction-sprung-from.
I: Whatever being has glory, splendor, or vigor, know each one to have sprung from a mere fraction of my splendor.
N: The reduplicated yat yat...tat tat, 'whatever...that', generalizes the whole preceding catalog: any vibhūtimat, 'glorious', śrīmat, 'splendid, fortunate', or ūrjitam, 'mighty' being anywhere, not only the named examples, springs from a mere aṃśa, 'fraction, portion', of Kṛṣṇa's own tejas, 'splendor' — the same tejas already claimed at v.36. Sandhi: श्रीमदूर्जितमेव packs śrīmat+ūrjitam (-t+ū-→-d ū-, a new instance of the dental-voicing-before-vowel pattern seen at tat+aham, tat+asti in v.39); तत्तदेवावगच्छ packs tat+tat (joined) +eva (-t+e-→-d e-) +avagaccha (a+a→ā); तेजोंऽशसंभवम् packs tejaḥ+aṃśa (-aḥ+a-→-o-, avagraha, with aṃśa's inherent nasal surviving).
#42
L: Or-rather, with-this-much known, what, for-you, Arjuna; having-propped-up-I this whole with-a-single-fraction, standing, the-world.
I: Or rather, what use to you is all this detailed knowledge, Arjuna? I stand sustaining this entire universe with a single fraction of myself.
N: The chapter's closing verse turns from the catalog itself to dismiss it: bahunā...jñātena, 'by this extensive knowledge', is waved off as beside the point, since the point was never the list's completeness but the single fact stated in the second line — viṣṭabhya, 'having propped up, sustained', governs idam kṛtsnam jagat, 'this entire universe', held up by Kṛṣṇa with a mere eka-aṃśena, 'a single portion', of himself, echoing and capping the aṃśa of v.41. Sandhi: बहुनैतेन packs bahunā+etena (ā+e→ai); तवार्जुन packs tava+arjuna (a+a→ā); विष्टभ्याहमिदं packs viṣṭabhya+aham (a+a→ā) +idam (joined, no change); कृत्स्नमेकांशेन packs kṛtsnam+ekāṃśena (joined, no change) with eka+aṃśena internally (a+a→ā); स्थितो shows -aḥ before j-→-o.
